messages:
Amy (support): FYI customer on Dedicated Private (Acme) reporting 401s only when traffic goes through their NLB -> Istio ingress. Direct hits to pods are fine. They say Authorization header is missing at our gateway. Repro steps attached, can someone triage?

Raj (eng-infra): Can you paste a raw curl -v showing the header and the server-side request headers? Also which LB type/annotations are they using? ALB vs NLB matters.

Amy (support): Here's a minimal repro they sent:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...customer-token..." https://acme-vip.example.com/api/v1/predict
* Connected to acme-vip.example.com (10.0.0.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /api/v1/predict HTTP/1.1
> Host: acme-vip.example.com
> Authorization: Bearer eyJ...customer-token...
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*

< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:10:34 GMT
< content-length: 45

{"error":"missing authorization header"}
```

And server-side request logged by our runtime (headers we see):

```
GET /api/v1/predict
Host: acme-vip.example.com
User-Agent: env-client/1.0
X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4
X-Request-Id: abc-123
# no Authorization header present
```

They added this NLB annotation: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: '*'` to preserve client IP. Behavior started after that change.

Lina (eng-platform): Ah — proxy protocol on NLB. NLB sends a PROXY header at the TCP level (v1/v2). If the ingress gateway (Envoy) isn't configured to accept PROXY protocol, the initial bytes look like garbage and can break how Envoy parses the request, which can look like header loss or connection errors.

Tom (eng-runtime): Agreed. Two quick checks: 1) Are they terminating TLS on the NLB or passing through? 2) Is Istio/Envoy configured with the PROXY protocol listener filter? If TLS is terminated at LB and re-originated to the gateway, headers SHOULD pass through intact — proxy-protocol is independent but must be understood by the listener.

Mia (customer-success): Customer confirms NLB is terminating TLS (listeners 443 -> instance: 443) and they enabled proxy-protocol to keep source IP. They rolled this change yesterday and errors started immediately.

Raj (eng-infra): That lines up. If NLB is terminating TLS and then speaking plain HTTP to Istio, the PROXY header is prepended and Envoy must have a listener filter to consume it. Otherwise the first bytes are the PROXY signature and Envoy will misparse the HTTP message. That can manifest as dropped headers or 400/401 depending on filters.

Amy (support): Ok what do we tell them to change? Fastest workaround?

Tom (eng-runtime): Two options:
- Disable proxy-protocol on the NLB (if they don't need source IP at that layer) — simplest.
- Enable PROXY protocol support on the Istio ingressgateway so Envoy can parse the PROXY header. This requires an EnvoyFilter to add the PROXY protocol listener filter on the gateway's listener.

Lina (eng-platform): Example EnvoyFilter we share often (customer-friendly):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: enable-proxy-protocol
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      istio: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: LISTENER
    match:
      listener:
        portNumber: 443
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager"
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        listener_filters:
        - name: "envoy.filters.listener.proxy_protocol"
```

(We usually include version-specific notes; customer may need to use v2 binary header support depending on NLB config.)

Raj (eng-infra): Also remind them that AWS NLB proxy-protocol is sometimes v2 by default, and older Envoy listener filters may expect v1. Confirm which proxy version they enabled.

Amy (support): I asked customer if they can toggle proxy-protocol off as a quick test. They responded: "Can try but need client IP for logging; prefer enabling proxy support on gateway if possible."

Tom (eng-runtime): OK. If they prefer enabling on gateway, give them the EnvoyFilter + a small checklist:
1) Confirm NLB proxy-protocol version (v1 vs v2).
2) Apply EnvoyFilter to istio-system and verify ingressgateway pods restart/roll.
3) Validate with curl -v again to VIP and check runtime logs for Authorization header.

Amy (support): I ran a quick local test with proxy-protocol toggled on and an Envoy instance without the listener filter — I saw similar missing headers. With the listener filter added, Authorization was preserved.

Mia (customer-success): Customer asked if we can make the change on their Dedicated cluster (we don't manage NLB annotations). They asked for exact commands to apply the EnvoyFilter.

Lina (eng-platform): Provide these kubectl commands:

```bash
kubectl apply -f enable-proxy-protocol-envoyfilter.yaml -n istio-system
kubectl rollout restart deploy/istio-ingressgateway -n istio-system
kubectl logs -l istio=ingressgateway -n istio-system --tail=200
```

And advise them to watch for crashloop or parsing errors in logs. If they see errors like "corrupted PROXY header", verify the proxy version.

Raj (eng-infra): Also mention an alternate workaround: switch to an ALB (Layer7) or do TCP passthrough (preserve TLS) so the LB doesn't inject PROXY headers or re-terminate TLS. But that has tradeoffs.

Amy (support): I'll send the EnvoyFilter + checklist to customer and request their proxy-protocol version. I'll reconvene after they test. Thanks all :pray: 

deploy-bot: Deployment of enable-proxy-protocol-envoyfilter.yaml to istio-system requested by Amy. Status: pending.

Tom (eng-runtime): If they hit edge cases, ask them to include a tcpdump of the first 128 bytes between LB and ingress (pcap) so we can inspect the exact PROXY frame.

Amy (support): Noted. I'll keep the thread updated.

(thumbsup reaction from Mia)
